events.summary: Strategy correction: an unactivated Tree of Perdition protects itself. Its ability is an instant-speed tap ability, so removal aimed at the Tree can be answered by activating in response — the exchange resolves first and sets the remover to the Tree's toughness. An untapped 0/13 Tree therefore deters removal from anyone above 13 life, while a spent 0/36 Tree is a plain wall that costs nothing to answer. Firing it on turn 7 locked in a 0/36 body and cashed the public promise, but traded away that deterrent and the option to exchange at instant speed later.

rules.point: Unused and untapped, the Tree taxes its own removal; spent, it is only a wall. Exchanging early maximizes the Tree’s toughness but gives up the deterrent.
